headline: A quiet week for competitors, but the open lanes got clearer: everyone is working on which ad goes in a scene and which clip to find, and nobody on where the break lands or how a viewer discovers what they can't describe.
summary: No competitor in the 40-odd companies tracked had verifiably new product news this week; search coverage was thin, so read this as 'not surfaced' rather than 'nothing published'.

New in the window: Parks finds 39% of US households watch live via on-demand streamers (22 Oct); Beet.TV pieces on Coactive and Omnicom (21–25 Oct) keep the CTV conversation on targeting and relevance, not break placement; Roku partners with IRIS.TV for show-level signals (22 Oct).
Scene-level metadata is moving into platforms (Bitmovin, Comcast, AWS, all September). The specialist argument shifts to depth and viewer outcomes.
Next 14 days: Satis (4–5 Nov, going, Embrace booth). DPP Leaders' Briefing follows on 17–18 Nov.
No new public mentions of Vionlabs found; TVBEurope award claim still unconfirmed. Several W43 mentions are still waiting for a reshare.

ideas.hook: 39% of US homes now watch live sports or events through on-demand streamers. Nobody has told those apps where the ad break goes in a live match or a news hour.
ideas.angle: Parks Associates' new report puts live inside on-demand apps at 39% of US internet households, with a quarter watching live via FAST. Live and news are where a badly timed break costs the most. The same scene-level understanding that finds a natural pause in a drama can find it in a news hour or a match.
ideas.proof: Ad-Break Creation and Contextual Ad-Breaks; news-broadcaster ICP. Needs a Vionlabs live or news example before posting; check what is public.

reactsTo.label: Research: 39% of US watch live content through streamers (Advanced Television)

ideas.hook: Scene-level targeting is a crowded shelf now. Scene-level break placement is an empty one.
ideas.angle: Coactive argues AI context unlocks ad inventory; Omnicom says two thirds of viewers avoid ads yet most feel favourable toward ads relevant to the content (both via Beet.TV snippets, verify numbers). Everyone is working on which ad goes in a scene. Few say where in the story the break should fall. Slides: what scene-level targeting does, what it leaves out, what a story-aware break adds.
ideas.proof: Ad-Break Creation and Contextual Ad-Breaks; the SDVI ad-break demo from IBC. Don't name competitors.
ideas.event: The Future of TV Advertising Global (8–9 Dec)

reactsTo.label: AI can unlock streaming's untapped advertising goldmine: Coactive's Cody Coleman (Beet.TV)
Two thirds of consumers are avoiding ads, but they're not anti-brand (Beet.TV)

ideas.hook: Every search box in video is learning to find the moment you already know exists. Viewers need the one they didn't know they wanted.
ideas.angle: This year's pitches from Valossa, Imaginario and others centre on asking for a clip in plain language. That is retrieval, and it works for editors who know what they're after. Discovery is the opposite problem: the viewer can't describe it. It needs the feel of a scene in the data, not a better prompt box. Acknowledge that retrieval is real value before arguing the difference.
ideas.proof: Mood rows and Similar Titles from Curio; an emotion curve for one title.

reactsTo.label: Valossa: Ask-First Video Editing (blog title seen via search)
Imaginario AI: find moments, not files (ISE 2026)

ideas.hook: Bitmovin, Comcast and AWS all shipped scene analysis in September. If scene metadata is becoming a platform feature, what's left for a specialist?
ideas.angle: A candid post about what happens when the big platforms add your category as a feature. The honest answer: depth, taste and proof on viewer outcomes. Where scene analysis tags what is on screen, a specialist has to say what it feels like and show it changed viewing. Credit the others for making the category real.
ideas.proof: Needs Arash's own view and one viewer-outcome number we can cite publicly.

reactsTo.label: Nine deploys Bitmovin AI Scene Analysis on Stan
Comcast Technology Solutions VideoAI workflow apps
AWS Elemental Inference: contextual metadata for live video

ideas.hook: TiVo's new assistant lets you search by mood. The interface is ready. Who is producing the mood data behind it?
ideas.angle: Natural-language, mood-aware search is arriving in the UI (Agent TiVo, announced 11 Sep per Advanced Television; verify). A query like 'something tense but warm' only works if scenes were described that way upstream. A question mark over the data layer, not a dig at TiVo.
ideas.proof: Scene-level emotion metadata and mood rows in Curio. Check the TiVo date on the page first.

reactsTo.label: Agent TiVo conversational discovery assistant (Advanced Television)

ideas.hook: Disney, Fox, Banijay and Yle are all commissioning vertical microdramas. What does a library owner do with the 4,000 titles they already have?
ideas.angle: Microdrama has moved from app category to commissioned format. The new money chases new vertical productions, but existing libraries hold plenty of scenes that already work as short, self-contained stories. The question is which ones, and how to choose without a human watching everything.
ideas.proof: Preview Clips & Shorts, selecting by emotional arc. Number '4,000' is illustrative: replace with a real library size or drop it.
ideas.event: Content London (30 Nov–3 Dec), if attending

reactsTo.label: Banijay's Brazilian prodcos forge microdrama pact (Broadcast)

ideas.hook: Sweden ended over 4 million streaming subscriptions in a year, and still hit a record of 11 million paying. Churn isn't leaving. It's the default.
ideas.angle: A Nordic angle from a Stockholm company. People leave and come back constantly, so the first ten minutes after they return decide the next month. What they see on the home screen matters more than the catalogue behind it.
ideas.proof: Curio for returning viewers; check for a newer Mediavision release first (this one is from April).

reactsTo.label: Sweden's paid streaming subscriptions hit a record 11 million (Mediavision, via Senal News)

coverage: Window: 2026-10-19 → 2026-10-26 (8 days since W43). This was a thin week: all six research scans found little or nothing verifiably dated inside the window, so most ideas build on September and early-October items plus a handful of items from 21–26 Oct.

Events come from content-engine/config/events.yaml (snapshot 2026-10-20) because the Notion connector is not enabled in this session. The snapshot may be stale: NAB New York is shown as recent but attendance was never confirmed.
The idea board was read-only checked: the work and team_ideas collections were empty, so nothing is excluded for being posted, parked or drafted.
WebFetch is blocked by DNS in this environment, so every finding comes from search-result summaries. Check exact quotes, dates and numbers on the source page before posting.
LinkedIn is login-walled and site:linkedin.com searches returned almost nothing. No public mention of Vionlabs dated 12 Oct or later was found; that is a search gap, not proof there were none.

Unconfirmed: TVBEurope Best of Show award (see mentions); the Roku/IRIS.TV, Coactive, Omnicom and Agent TiVo items rest on snippets; Marengo 3.5 and TwelveLabs subscription pricing dates are unverified and left out; the 24i sale has no primary source and is left out.

Not reached: Wurl, FreeWheel, Qvest, Valossa, Mimir, Moments Lab, DeepVA, PA TV Metadata newsrooms; Nielsen Gauge Aug/Sep, Antenna Q3, BBC/ITVX/C4/RTL/SVT news. Competitor entries other than IRIS.TV and Coactive are carried from W43 with no new items found.
Search budget: each agent used 11–28 of its 30.
Research agents were given 30-search budgets; the discovery agent used only 12 and the CTV agent 11, so quiet companies had thin coverage. A run with direct page access would likely surface more.
